correctness.rationale: For each point, the least visible return is its exact cycle length if at most d; otherwise its d+1 terms are all distinct. In the absence of cross equalities, the ordered pair of these visible periods determines the type, yielding (d+1)^2 choices. A short common cycle of length L contributes its L distinct offsets. On a common cycle of length L>d, the set of true cross differences is one residue class intersected with [-d,d]. It has at most two entries since 2L>2d; a doubleton recovers its exact separation L and has 2d+1-L possibilities for d<L<=2d. Singletons give 2d+1 distinct types, all realized at L=2d+1. This gives 2d^2+5d+2 and includes coincident points. Two copies of every short period are forced by the equal-period no-cross requirement. Each intermediate cycle is forced by its doubleton, and the singleton {d} forces L>=2d+1 or else d-L is visible as well. Adding forced sizes gives (d+1)(5d+2)/2. The proposed cycle union realizes every cross type and has two distinct long cycles for the long/long no-cross type (also when d=1); at equality no other cycle is possible. Independently ran `python audit_checks/independent_replays.py 2`, evaluating literal iterates as ordered equality partitions. Counts 9,20,35,54,77 and sizes 7,18,34,55,81 matched at depths 1–5; exhaustive integer partitions through the proposed minimum gave exactly one universal cycle profile at depths 1 and 2. This bounded test is not the all-depth proof. The submitted verifier was inspected, not executed.
